source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Animal Diversity I: Invertebrate Phyla
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Animals in which the body cavity is lined on all sides by mesoderm are described as
questions.explanation: A true coelom (eucoelom) is a mesoderm-lined cavity, as in annelids, arthropods and chordates.

questions.stem: Choanocytes (collar cells) that drive the water current occur in
questions.explanation: Flagellated choanocytes line sponge canals and trap food particles.

questions.stem: Stinging cells used for offence and defence in Hydra are called
questions.explanation: Cnidoblasts containing nematocysts are the diagnostic cells of Cnidaria.

questions.stem: Eight external comb plates used in locomotion are characteristic of
questions.explanation: Ctenophores (comb jellies) swim with eight rows of ciliated comb plates.

questions.stem: Flame cells (protonephridia) for osmoregulation and excretion are found in
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes are acoelomate and use flame cells; earthworms have nephridia.

questions.stem: Roundworms such as Ascaris possess a body cavity that is
options: a pseudocoelom not fully lined by mesoderm
questions.explanation: Aschelminthes (Nematoda) are pseudocoelomate; the cavity is a persistent blastocoel.

questions.stem: Metameric segmentation and a closed blood vascular system occur together in
questions.explanation: Annelids (e.g. Pheretima, Nereis) are metameric eucoelomates with closed circulation.

questions.stem: Jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton are diagnostic of
questions.explanation: Arthropoda is the largest phylum; the name means jointed legs, and the cuticle is chitinous.

questions.stem: The rasping feeding organ called a radula is present in
questions.explanation: A chitinous radula is the typical molluscan feeding structure (absent in bivalves).

questions.stem: The water vascular (ambulacral) system used in locomotion is unique to
questions.explanation: Tube feet of starfish and other echinoderms are operated by the water vascular system.

questions.stem: The stomochord of Balanoglossus is a structure of the
questions.explanation: Hemichordates have a buccal diverticulum (stomochord) in the proboscis, not a true notochord.

questions.stem: Alternation of a sessile polyp and a free-swimming medusa generation (metagenesis) is typical of
questions.explanation: Obelia (Cnidaria) shows metagenesis: asexual polyps and sexual medusae in the life cycle.

questions.stem: Which combination of phylum and distinctive feature is incorrect?
options: Arthropoda — haemocoel and Malpighian tubules in many insects
Echinodermata — closed circulation and bilateral adult
questions.explanation: Adult echinoderms are pentamerous radial; larvae are bilateral. Circulation is not a typical closed blood system like annelids.

questions.stem: Triploblastic, bilateral, acoelomate animals belong to
questions.explanation: Flatworms have three germ layers and no body cavity; cnidarians are diploblastic.

questions.stem: Sycon, Spongilla and Euspongia are examples of
questions.explanation: These genera are sponges with a canal system and skeleton of spicules or spongin.

questions.stem: Physalia, Adamsia, Pennatula and Meandrina are placed in
questions.explanation: Portuguese man-of-war, sea anemone, sea pen and brain coral are cnidarians.

questions.stem: Pleurobrachia and Ctenoplana are marine animals that exhibit
questions.explanation: These are ctenophores; they lack nematocysts of cnidarians and swim with comb plates.

questions.stem: Planaria, Fasciola and Taenia share which feature?
options: Dorsoventrally flattened, mostly parasitic or free-living acoelomates
questions.explanation: They are platyhelminths: flat, triploblastic and without a coelom; many are parasites.

questions.stem: Ancylostoma and Wuchereria are members of
questions.explanation: Hookworm and filarial worm are roundworms with a pseudocoelom and a complete alimentary canal.

questions.stem: Nereis, Pheretima and Hirudinaria belong to a phylum that is
options: radial as adults with tube feet
questions.explanation: Clamworm, earthworm and leech are annelids with true coelom and serial segmentation.

questions.stem: Limulus, Locusta, Apis and Palaemon are all
questions.explanation: King crab, locust, honeybee and prawn have jointed legs and a chitinous exoskeleton.

questions.stem: Sepia, Octopus, Pinctada and Dentalium are examples of
questions.explanation: Cuttlefish, octopus, pearl oyster and tusk shell are molluscs with a mantle covering the visceral mass.

questions.stem: Asterias, Echinus, Antedon and Cucumaria belong to a phylum whose adults are
options: pentamerous radial with a calcareous endoskeleton
questions.explanation: Starfish, sea urchin, sea lily and sea cucumber are echinoderms; larvae are bilateral.

questions.stem: The larva of Balanoglossus that resembles an echinoderm larva is the
questions.explanation: Tornaria of hemichordates is similar to the bipinnaria of echinoderms, supporting a deuterostome link.

questions.stem: Open circulatory system with haemocoel is a feature of
questions.explanation: Arthropods and most molluscs have an open system; annelids and vertebrates have a closed system.

questions.stem: Among invertebrate phyla, which statement is incorrect?
options: Sponges are hermaphrodite and show internal fertilisation in many species
Cnidarians are diploblastic with a gastrovascular cavity
Nematodes are dioecious with sexual dimorphism often marked
Hemichordates possess a true notochord throughout life
questions.explanation: The stomochord is not a notochord; hemichordates are a separate invertebrate phylum.
